title: DISC Assessment
subtitle: Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, Conscientiousness
description: Measures four core dimensions of behavior to understand communication, teamwork, and task styles.

questions.text: When facing a major challenge or obstacle, what is your immediate response?

options.text: Take charge directly and focus on a fast, decisive solution.
Gather people together to discuss, motivate, and brainstorm.
Step back, remain calm, and work methodically to maintain stability.
Analyze all data and details thoroughly before making a precise plan.

questions.text: How would others most likely describe your communication style?

options.text: Direct, assertive, and results-oriented.
Enthusiastic, persuasive, and outgoing.
Patient, supportive, and an active listener.
Diplomatic, analytical, and detail-focused.

questions.text: In a team or group project, which role do you naturally fall into?

options.text: The driver who sets targets and pushes for completion.
The promoter who builds relationships and keeps energy high.
The reliable team player who coordinates and supports others.
The quality checker who ensures standards and accuracy are met.

questions.text: What is your biggest fear or source of discomfort at work or school?

options.text: Losing control, lack of progress, or wasting time.
Social rejection, isolation, or being ignored.
Sudden changes, instability, or conflict.
Making mistakes, low standards, or lack of clear guidelines.

questions.text: What motivates you the most to excel?

options.text: Independence, power, and achieving major results.
Recognition, praise, and connecting with others.
Cooperation, security, and a peaceful environment.
Precision, quality work, and gaining deep expertise.

questions.text: When communicating in writing (email or chat), what is your primary focus?

options.text: Brief, bullet-pointed, and focused only on action items.
Friendly, expressive, using exclamation marks or emojis.
Polite, supportive, and checking in on their well-being.
Formal, highly detailed, and grammatically precise.

questions.text: How do you handle team members who are highly emotional or upset?

options.text: Encourage them to focus on tasks and keep moving forward.
Listen actively, offer positive encouragement, and lift spirits.
Provide a safe, quiet space and express genuine empathy.
Help them analyze the situation logically to find a solution.

questions.text: What is your typical pace of working and making decisions?

options.text: Fast-paced, action-oriented, willing to take calculated risks.
Spontaneous, energetic, guided by intuition and inspiration.
Steady, deliberate, preferring a predictable step-by-step pace.
Slow, methodical, verifying facts and quality thoroughly.

title: Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI)
subtitle: 16 Psychological Personalities
description: Evaluates your preferences across four core cognitive dichotomies to identify one of the 16 personality types.

questions.text: After a busy and socially active week, how do you recharge your energy?

options.text: By spending time with friends, going out, or socializing.
By spending quiet time alone, reading, or relaxing in private.

questions.text: When in a social gathering, do you usually...

text.text: Start conversations with many people, including strangers.
Keep conversations to a few people you already know well.

questions.text: When learning a new subject, what type of information appeals to you more?

text.text: Practical facts, concrete details, and real-world examples.
General concepts, theoretical models, and future possibilities.

questions.text: You tend to trust...

text.text: Direct experience, solid evidence, and historical data.
Your gut feelings, subtle patterns, and creative insights.

questions.text: When making a difficult decision, what do you prioritize?

text.text: Logical analysis, objective truth, and fairness.
Impact on people, personal values, and harmony.

questions.text: How do others view your decision-making style?

text.text: Reasonable, analytical, and sometimes tough-minded.
Warm, empathetic, and sensitive to feelings.

questions.text: How do you prefer to manage your daily schedule and tasks?

text.text: Having a clear plan, checking off checklists, and avoiding last-minute rushes.
Remaining flexible, adapting to opportunities, and working under pressure.

questions.text: Your work and study spaces are typically...

text.text: Organized, neat, and highly structured.
Relaxed, organic, and occasionally messy.

questions.text: When working on a project, do you prefer to...

text.text: Brainstorm out loud with a collaborative group.
Process ideas internally first before sharing them.

questions.text: If you had to describe your approach to problem-solving, is it more...

text.text: Grounded in realistic steps and practical constraints.
Focused on creative concepts and innovative possibilities.

questions.text: In a team disagreement, is it more important to be...

text.text: Truthful, direct, and logically consistent.
Tactful, supportive, and maintain team morale.

questions.text: When planning a holiday or trip, do you prefer...

text.text: A detailed, structured itinerary with pre-booked slots.
A loose plan, leaving room for spontaneous exploration.

title: Personality Factor Questionnaire
subtitle: 16PF Career Matching
description: Evaluates your primary work, thinking, and communication styles to map you to optimal career paths.

questions.text: How do you approach complex problems requiring long-term analysis?

options.text: Break it down systematically and work in absolute quiet.
Collaborate immediately with others and experiment actively.
Follow established guidelines and trusted standards.

questions.text: When team roles are being assigned, you typically prefer:

options.text: Direct leadership, setting strategic goals.
Execution, ensuring all tasks conform strictly to rules.
Facilitating communication and helping resolve disputes.

questions.text: If a project plan changes suddenly at the last minute, you:

options.text: Adapt quickly and enjoy the challenge of finding new ways.
Feel anxious or stressed about the lack of structured planning.
Quietly double-check the logic of the change before acting.

questions.text: In terms of personal reflection and internal thinking:

options.text: You frequently daydream and analyze philosophical ideas.
You focus strictly on realistic, practical, hands-on tasks.

questions.text: When working in stressful conditions, you remain:

options.text: Calm, emotionally stable, and focused on the big picture.
Sensitive, highly alert, and reactive to details.

questions.text: If you observe a colleague violating minor company guidelines, what do you do?

options.text: Remind them of the guidelines or notify a supervisor.
Ignore it as long as the work quality remains good.
Gently mention it in private to help them avoid trouble.

questions.text: When learning a highly complex technical software or theory, you prefer:

options.text: Reading the technical documentation and manual step-by-step.
Opening the tool and learning through trial and error.

questions.text: In social gatherings, do you prefer to be:

options.text: Directly engaging with others, making warm connections.
Reserved, observing the social environment carefully.

title: Eysenck Personality Inventory
subtitle: EPI Temperament Scales
description: Evaluates your biological temperament across Extraversion (E) and Neuroticism (N) scales to map to standard temperaments.

questions.text: Do you tend to keep in the background on social occasions?

options.text: No, you love being active and part of the conversation.
Yes, you prefer to stay quiet and observe.

questions.text: Does your mood often go up and down without any obvious reason?

options.text: Yes, your emotions fluctuate quite frequently.
No, you are generally emotionally steady and calm.

questions.text: Would you say that you are a highly lively and talkative person?

options.text: Absolutely, you talk a lot and express energy.
Not really, you are reserved and think before talking.

questions.text: Do you often worry about things that you should not have done or said?

options.text: Yes, you dwell on conversations and worry a lot.
No, you let go of things easily and do not worry.

questions.text: When things go wrong, do you easily lose your temper or get upset?

options.text: Yes, you react intensely and feel stressed.
No, you stay cool and handle it calmly.

questions.text: Do you usually make decisions on the spur of the moment?

options.text: Yes, you prefer fast, spontaneous action.
No, you take your time to weigh options carefully.

questions.text: Do you often feel 'fed up' or down for no reason?

options.text: Yes, you feel emotional shifts quite easily.
No, your mood is generally positive and steady.

questions.text: Are you a person who loves exciting, high-stimulation activities?

options.text: Absolutely, you seek thrills and active fun.
Not really, you prefer low-key, peaceful pastimes.

title: Enneagram Core Test
subtitle: 9 Interconnected Personality Types
description: Uncovers your core motivations, deepest fears, and developmental pathways among the 9 archetypes.

questions.text: What is your deepest core desire or ultimate goal in life?

options.text: To be perfect, upright, and have high moral standards.
To feel loved, helpful, and deeply appreciated.
To be successful, admired, and highly productive.
To be unique, authentic, and understand your deep feelings.

questions.text: How do you typically react when a problem arises?

options.text: Analyze it intellectually, seeking knowledge.
Anticipate risks, seek security, and consult systems.
Avoid pain, find fun alternatives and solutions.
Take direct control and defend your boundaries.
Keep the peace and go with the flow.

questions.text: When working in a team, you feel most comfortable when:

options.text: Everything is organized correctly and matches high standards.
You can support members and ensure warmth.
The team is hitting goals and achieving milestones.
The project allows for personal expression and uniqueness.

questions.text: Your attitude towards rules and security is usually:

options.text: You question them intellectually to find the absolute truth.
You respect rules for safety but prepare for the worst.
You view rules as limiting and seek variety.
You make your own rules and resist control.

questions.text: If someone disagrees with you, your immediate reaction is to:

options.text: Correct them with facts and objective logic.
Adapt or compromise to preserve a peaceful relationship.
Assert your position strongly and engage in debate.
Feel personally misunderstood or unique.

questions.text: What is your biggest fear or source of vulnerability?

options.text: Being corrupt, defective, or failing standards.
Being unwanted, unloved, or unhelpful.
Being overwhelmed, helpless, or incompetent.
Lacking support, guidance, or security.

questions.text: How do you view success and productivity?

options.text: My primary goal is to be highly efficient, achieve milestones, and gain status.
I care more about authentic expression than cold, efficient metrics.
I value freedom and experiencing exciting new ideas or options.
I prefer a harmonious, comfortable pace where everyone feels included.

questions.text: When facing a major team challenge, your natural reaction is to:

options.text: Directly confront the problem, make firm decisions, and take charge.
Identify potential risks, build a secure backup plan, and seek team alignment.
Research all technical background data in detail to find the optimal solution.
Focus on how the team is feeling and make sure everyone is supported.

questions.text: How do you typically handle emotional pain or frustration?

options.text: Refocus on exciting plans, positive thoughts, and fun activities.
Sit with my feelings, explore their unique meaning, and seek depth.
Control my emotional reactions and focus on doing what is correct.
Calm down, withdraw to maintain peace, and avoid dwelling on the conflict.

title: Caliper Profile
subtitle: Job Performance Matching
description: Aligns your cognitive styles and personal drivers directly with high-performance job domains and organizational roles.

questions.text: How do you handle persuading someone who initially disagrees with you?

options.text: Listen deeply to understand their needs, then adjust your pitch.
Present powerful facts, speak assertively, and push for agreement.
Feel highly energized by the challenge of winning them over.
Find a structured, standard policy to settle the argument.

questions.text: When managing multiple tasks with tight deadlines, you:

options.text: Excel at shifting focus dynamically and taking quick risks.
Methodically schedule each hour and avoid any deviations.
Take absolute responsibility and direct others on what to do.

questions.text: In terms of analyzing data and logical systems, you:

options.text: Love solving abstract puzzles and identifying hidden patterns.
Prefer practical, hands-on application over abstract theories.

questions.text: What keeps you going after experiencing a significant setback?

options.text: The strong inner desire to prove your capability and win.
Having a supportive team and maintaining stable workflows.

questions.text: When presenting your ideas in a public meeting, you:

options.text: Express yourself with high confidence and relish the attention.
Write down a detailed script in advance to ensure total accuracy.

questions.text: When you are in a team discussion about a new project idea, you usually:

options.text: Are the first to speak, sharing your ideas with confidence.
Listen first, taking detailed notes before expressing a view.

questions.text: When a process or workflow is repetitive and routine, you:

options.text: Thrive in the consistency and predictable quality of the routine.
Feel restless and seek ways to innovate or automate the steps.

questions.text: How do you handle client or customer interactions?

options.text: Focus heavily on understanding their underlying feelings and concerns.
Focus on the objective agreement, presenting persuasive advantages to close.

title: Minnesota Multiphasic Test
subtitle: MMPI Clinical Insights
description: Evaluates your psychological coping capacity, emotional stability, and behavioral tendencies under stress.

questions.text: Under high academic or professional pressure, how do you feel physically?

options.text: You frequently develop headaches, fatigue, or stomach discomfort.
Your physical state remains stable; you manage stress mentally.

questions.text: Do you occasionally feel like people around you are critical or talking about you?

options.text: Yes, you often feel defensive and suspicious of others' motives.
No, you rarely worry about what others say or think behind your back.

questions.text: How would you describe your level of daily energy and excitement?

options.text: Extremely high; you often take on too many projects and speak rapidly.
Steady and balanced; you work at a sustainable, moderate pace.
Often quite low; you struggle with motivation and feel downcast.

questions.text: When in a social setting, how comfortable do you feel interacting?

options.text: You feel extremely anxious, prefer to stay alone, and avoid crowds.
You are highly comfortable, outgoing, and thrive in group environments.

questions.text: How often do you find yourself double-checking your actions, thoughts, or doors?

options.text: Constantly; you worry excessively about mistakes and small details.
Occasionally or normally; you trust your actions and move on quickly.

questions.text: Do you find yourself experiencing sudden worries or fears without any clear cause?

options.text: Yes, you feel anxious or hyper-vigilant quite often.
No, you feel calm, trusting your environment.

questions.text: Do you struggle with feeling disconnected from others, even when in a group?

options.text: Yes, you feel isolated or misunderstood by most people.
No, you feel deeply connected and adapt easily to group vibes.

questions.text: When you are very busy or excited, do you find it hard to rest or sleep?

options.text: Yes, your mind races with too many ideas and plans.
No, you can easily wind down and maintain healthy rest.
